person.name: Matthew Liu
person.headline: I build the systems that keep intelligent software honest.
person.introduction: Working across AI evaluation, observability, and infrastructure, I turn ideas and research into production services built to scale, endure, and evolve.

path.organization: Johns Hopkins Whiting School of Engineering
path.summary: Learning across systems thinking, research, and building.
Production model-customization workflows spanning preparation, training, evaluation, and deployment.
Systems that make agent behavior inspectable and easier to improve.

projects.title: UCredit
projects.question: Can degree planning feel less uncertain?
projects.description: A collaborative advising dashboard built on uCredit to help students and advisors reason about academic plans.

projects.title: Model Customization Assistant
projects.question: Can model training begin with intent, not infrastructure?
projects.description: An agent-guided SageMaker workflow that turns a use case into data preparation, fine-tuning, evaluation, and deployment steps.

projects.title: LLM-as-a-Judge
projects.question: How should a model judge work it cannot see all at once?
projects.description: Evaluation work that turns long agent traces into structured, evidence-linked assessments using raw context, compact digests, and anchored verdicts.
projects.contribution: Evaluation UX, judging architecture, and implementation

projects.title: Weave Agent Adapter
projects.question: What did the agent actually do?
projects.description: An adapter that turns agent activity into inspectable traces across multiple coding environments.

projects.title: Monopole
projects.question: Can agents learn from completed work?
projects.description: A local evaluation workspace for reviewing completed agent runs and turning evidence into better future behavior.
projects.contribution: Product direction, evaluation design, and implementation
